title: Well Crank

serves.summary: The learner picks a wheel size on a well so a weak animal can wind up a bucket, which shows that a bigger wheel on the same axle takes less push to turn.

request.topic: Wheel and axle: a bigger wheel takes less push to turn
request.objective: A bigger wheel on the same axle takes less push to turn, so a weak pusher can lift a load with a big wheel that it cannot lift with a small knob. (SCI005-01-d)

problems.ask: Help the mouse wind up the bucket. Tap a wheel on the well to let the mouse try.
problems.goal: The big wheel is on the axle: the mouse's push times the big wheel's radius (1 x 4) is at least the full bucket times the axle (3 x 1). The knob (1) and the middle wheel (2) are too small for the mouse.

problems.ask: Help the bear and the mouse each wind up a bucket.
problems.goal: The knob is on the bear's well and the big wheel on the mouse's well. The bear is strong enough to turn either (4 x 1 >= 3); the mouse can only turn the big wheel (1 x 4 >= 3).

problems.ask: Help the mouse wind up the bucket of rocks.
problems.goal: The big thin wooden wheel is on the axle (1 x 4 >= 4). The thick metal wheel looks strong but is small (1 x 1.5 < 4); the middle wheel is too small too (1 x 2 < 4). What a wheel is made of does not decide how hard it is to turn; its size does.

problems.ask: Help both mice wind up their buckets.
problems.goal: The middle wheel is on the half-full bucket's well (1 x 2 >= 2) and the big wheel on the rocks' well (1 x 4 >= 4). The bigger wheel has to go to the heavier bucket; the knob lifts neither.
